short_summary: A Tel Aviv University study reveals that Israeli grocery prices rose nearly five times faster between 2022 and 2026 than in the preceding four years. Researchers attribute the broad inflation to diminished public scrutiny and weak regulatory oversight.

sources.name: Ynet
sources.title: שוקולד פרה, קפה נמס ובורקס מעדנות: המוצרים שמחירם זינק בסופר

paragraphs: Over the past four years, Israeli grocery shoppers have faced an unprecedented acceleration in retail food prices. According to an extensive study led by Professor Itai Ater and doctoral candidate Adi Omer at Tel Aviv University's Coller School of Management, the cost of a standard grocery basket escalated nearly five times faster between September 2022 and August 2026 than it did during the preceding four-year interval.

The researchers analyzed price movements across roughly 700 supermarket branches, monitoring a standardized selection of 80 widely purchased items via data gathered under Israel's Food Law through the Pricez platform. Their findings indicate that after four years of relative price stability from September 2018 to August 2022, an aggressive inflationary cycle commenced in 2023 and persisted relentlessly through 2024 and 2025.

This inflationary burden has permeated every retail format, translating into hundreds of additional shekels on monthly household expenditures. Neighborhood convenience stores—such as Tiv Ta'am ba-City, Freshmarket, Shufersal Sheli, and Carrefour City—recorded a 19.6 percent surge, compared with a modest 4.3 percent rise in the previous period. Online grocery platforms experienced a 19 percent increase, sharply diverging from historical discount benchmarks. Even traditional discount supermarkets recorded an aggregate climb of 14.5 percent, contrasted with a mere 2.8 percent increase between 2018 and 2022.

Individual retail chains exhibited pronounced discrepancies. At Shufersal Deal, the monitored basket soared by 22.7 percent, tacking on 231 shekels, compared to an increase of just six shekels in the comparative earlier era. Shufersal Sheli and Freshmarket both registered 19.6 percent increases, while Victory marked a 16 percent rise. Rami Levy and Yohananof maintained relatively restrained trajectories, climbing 10.3 percent and 8.5 percent respectively, with Rami Levy preserving its status as the most economical chain.

Everyday pantry staples suffered remarkable leaps. A 100-gram bar of Elite cow milk chocolate surged by 77.9 percent in urban stores and 57.6 percent in discount aisles. A 200-gram jar of Taster's Choice freeze-dried instant coffee climbed by 26.1 percent in neighborhood outlets, and Ma'adanot cheese bourekas escalated by 30.9 percent in city branches following years of prior price declines.

Examining the underlying drivers, the researchers acknowledged rising value-added tax rates, municipal levies, and energy expenses, alongside price hikes on government-regulated items. However, they stressed that macroeconomic factors—including a stronger shekel and dropping international agricultural commodity prices—should theoretically have dampened domestic retail costs. They concluded that production and import pressures alone cannot justify an overarching 20 percent inflation rate, identifying a void in regulatory intervention and public discourse as the primary catalyst. With public focus directed elsewhere, suppliers and retailers capitalized on the absence of scrutiny.

Conversely, an industry retailer disputed these conclusions, arguing to Ynet that escalating labor expenses represent a decisive cost driver overlooked by the authors. The retailer also highlighted that select staple goods, including olive oil, frozen fish, and canned tuna, have actually become cheaper.

facts.fact: A study by Prof. Itai Ater and PhD candidate Adi Omer from Tel Aviv University tracked a basket of 80 popular items across roughly 700 supermarket branches using Pricez data under the Food Law.
Between September 2022 and August 2026, grocery basket prices climbed nearly five times faster than during the prior four-year period from September 2018 to August 2022.
Across neighborhood branches, the basket increased by 19.6% compared to 4.3% previously; online purchases rose 19% versus 4.1%; and discount chains rose 14.5% versus 2.8%.
Shufersal Deal saw a 22.7% basket jump (adding 231 shekels), while Rami Levy and Yohananof experienced more moderate increases of 10.3% and 8.5% respectively.
Prominent individual price spikes included Elite milk chocolate rising up to 77.9% in neighborhood stores and Ma'adanot cheese bourekas climbing 30.9% in city branches.

Researchers argued cost-of-production increases cannot fully account for the broad 20% surge, citing a regulatory and public vacuum, whereas a retailer argued rising labor costs were a critical neglected factor.
